skills_tools_canon.record: THE PROPOSED RULING, embodied in the built piece (script v3 ⚠ box + scene build): 'the boundary is the mechanism' — a tool is a connection the model calls: it reaches outside the model and ACTS in the world (proposed calls executed only as permitted); a skill is know-how the harness carries — a packaged way of working, held as durable files — that never acts itself; it GUIDES how the model works. Tools act. Skills guide. It lives in the piece at L6 ('A skill is different: know-how the system carries — it guides, it never acts') and in L3's one reworded word ('connection' handed to the model, canon §1's own gloss, replacing i2's bare 'capability'). Status in the script of record: PROVISIONAL — derived by exhaustion search of Hadi's own library (The Language of Agents vocabulary essay; the Academy study's site-grounded resolution; canon §1/§2/§3 — full trail in script v3's ⚠ box), shipped inside the artifact for Hadi to correct on it under his substantial-artifact rule; the bare gate (Action #28) was withdrawn and canon §6 O-1 stays open until his word lands here. The objectives audit's 'Partial' alignment read for this piece traces to exactly this layer. If he rules otherwise, L6 (and L3's one word) are the only lines that move, and L6 re-voices (board extra_check). This is the piece's primary open ask: board next_move = Action #28; primary_request = req-canon-o1-skills-tools.

story_structure.value: Problem–Agitation–Solution (urgency), declared before drafting because this definition is about a gap (saying vs doing) and PAS is the gap-shaped structure. PROBLEM: the model can only make words (L1–L2). AGITATION: perfect words that still do nothing — the email sits unsent. SOLUTION: a tool — the model asks, the tool acts, permission decides (L3–L9). The locked script's HS-09 reads the same arc as an S-11 misconception-correction: the viewer's existing model ('the AI sends my emails') is the thing being reassigned. Intended feeling: the invisible hand revealed — 'every time it just did it, there was a hand I never saw.'
